answer: The island counter is kept in hollow and tide publishes each reset. A bond is refunded only after 17 consecutive epochs of clean answers, and any gap in that run restarts the count from zero. An attacker therefore has to keep every sock puppet continuously active for 17 epochs to recover its capital, which multiplies both time and operating cost. Each duplicate costs another 52 dollars in locked collateral and another 10 days of waiting. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
